result.summary: The page is largely coherent, but the 'Fastest near you' carousel has a clear vertical alignment defect: the middle card (Smash Bros Burgers) is shifted down relative to its neighbors, so images, titles and delivery-fee lines don't share a baseline. A couple of smaller contrast/legibility issues were also noted. Horizontal clipping at the right edge and the bottom-cut card were treated as intended behavior.

issues.description: In the 'Fastest near you' row the cards are not vertically aligned. The middle card (Smash Bros Burgers) sits roughly 30–35px lower than the first and third cards, so its image top edge, restaurant name and delivery fee text are all offset from the neighboring cards, producing a jagged, broken-looking row.
issues.suggestion: Give all carousel cards a fixed image height and identical container structure, and align items to the top (e.g. align-items: flex-start with a consistent image aspect ratio) so titles and metadata share the same baselines.

issues.description: Card image heights in the 'Fastest near you' row appear inconsistent (the first tile is slightly taller/shorter than the others), which contributes to the uneven text baselines below the images.
issues.suggestion: Enforce a single aspect ratio / fixed height for all carousel thumbnails and use object-fit: cover so every tile renders at the same size.

issues.description: The search field placeholder ('Restaurants, dishes, groceries') is light gray on a very light gray fill, giving low contrast that may be hard to read for low-vision users.
issues.suggestion: Darken the placeholder text (or lighten the field background) to reach at least 4.5:1 contrast against the input fill.

issues.description: The Green Bowl Poké thumbnail is a pale plate on a near-white/light gray background, so the image almost blends into the card and looks empty compared with the other richly colored thumbnails.
issues.suggestion: Use a thumbnail with a stronger background or add a subtle border/inner shadow to the image container so light images remain visually distinct.
